atlas-lu.0060: Employers are used to hiring non-residents, but a non-EU graduate needs a permit. The EU Blue Card asks for a gross salary of at least €65,652 a year (for applications from 3 March 2026), a contract of at least 6 months and the qualifications the job needs. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-lu.0061: A photo is not required; it is acceptable in some sectors and many international companies expect none. Expatica still advises a passport-sized photo, top right.
atlas-lu.0062: One A4 page, or one to two pages; entry-level candidates can stay on one, and a second page is for highly qualified or experienced people. Write it in the language of the job posting and list language levels on the CEFR scale.
atlas-lu.0063: A concise cover letter explaining your motivation and what you would bring to the role is recommended, submitted with the CV through the online portal or by email.
atlas-lu.0064: Some companies ask for references from previous employers early; others ask for additional documents such as diplomas or references later. Keep reference letters ready in English and/or French.
atlas-lu.0065: Include a copy of your diploma if you studied in Luxembourg; list each degree with institution, country and year, and expect foreign documents to need a certified translation in some cases.
atlas-lu.0066: Salary is usually discussed in the first or second interview stage, often with the interviewer asking about your expectations; research typical pay first.
atlas-lu.0067: Employers can ask for diplomas and references at a later stage, and a language level may be tested in the interview; the pages read describe no routine background screening.
atlas-lu.0068: Applications to the large firms work through their portals and events; the EIB considers only applications for advertised positions. Networking also helps with smaller employers.
atlas-lu.0069: Employers are used to hiring people from abroad and from across the border: about 47% of employees are cross-border commuters and another 26% are foreign residents.
atlas-lu.0070: English and French for the Big Four; French, German or Luxembourgish for about half of all postings in one recruiter’s estimate (English named by the other half), and all three administrative languages for the civil service.
atlas-lu.0071: Expect four or five rounds of phone, online and in-person interviews of about 30 to 60 minutes each; confirm the interview language in advance and use formal address ("vous") in French. Deloitte and KPMG start with an online assessment of analytical skills and then hold several interviews.
atlas-lu.0072: The EIB process is screening, interview and additional tests for shortlisted candidates, then an offer; only applications for advertised positions are considered.
atlas-lu.0073: Civil service posts need a competitive exam: in general administration the general aptitude test (EAG) stays valid for 5 years, followed by a ministry-specific test for each post; language tests in Luxembourgish, French and German come first.
atlas-lu.0074: Probation is 2 weeks at least and at most 6 months for graduates (3 months for those without a CATP/DAP-level qualification, 12 months from a high gross monthly salary, €4,938.75 in the source read); it must be in the contract, and during the first 2 weeks neither side can end it without agreement.
atlas-lu.0075: After probation, an employer’s notice is 2 months under 5 years of service, 4 months from 5 to under 10 years and 6 months from 10 years; an employee’s notice when resigning is 1, 2 or 3 months for the same bands. Severance applies from 5 years of service.
atlas-lu.0076: Salary is discussed in the first or second interview, usually when the interviewer asks your expectations; check the contract for any thirteenth month, since the pages read do not state one.
atlas-lu.0077: Employers hire widely from abroad: about 47% of employees commute across the border and another 26% are foreign residents, so recruiters are used to cross-border and relocation questions.
atlas-lu.0078: For non-EU graduates the highly qualified route is the EU Blue Card: a gross salary of at least €65,652 a year for applications from 3 March 2026, a contract of at least 6 months and the qualifications the job needs. A job below that pay level needs a different permit.
atlas-lu.0079: What an employer wants to hear is that your right to work is settled or how it will be: say it in the first message, with the contract length and pay the Blue Card needs.
atlas-lu.0080: Boards and agencies: jobs.lu (English, French and German pages, with Graduate and Internship categories), Moovijob (including the Moovijob Day fair) and the national employment agency ADEM; civil service posts on GovJobs.lu.
atlas-lu.0081: Employers to look up: the Big Four’s Luxembourg offices, the European Investment Bank (job portal erecruitment.eib.org, traineeships and GRAD programmes) and the CSSF careers site.
atlas-lu.0082: Applying in the wrong language: write the CV and letter in the language of the job posting, and do not overstate your language level, which may be tested in the interview.
atlas-lu.0083: Missing the internship window: a practical internship after a Bachelor or BTS must fall wholly within 12 months after the last enrolment, so waiting a year loses the route.
atlas-lu.0084: Assuming the civil service is open in English: candidates must show sufficient Luxembourgish, French and German, and some posts need Luxembourg nationality.
atlas-lu.0085: The Big Four describe fluency in English and French as essential, and German or Luxembourgish as improving prospects.
atlas-lu.0086: English is the main working language in the financial sector; the national picture is mixed, with French, German or Luxembourgish named in about half of all postings in one recruiter’s April 2026 estimate and English in the other half.
atlas-lu.0087: IT roles sit in banks, fund administrators and the Big Four, where English is enough in most.
atlas-lu.0088: The civil service requires sufficient knowledge of Luxembourgish, French and German, at a level that depends on the pay group; the EIB asks for English and/or French.
atlas-lu.0089: ADEM counted more than 21,000 resident job seekers registered in 2025 and handled more than 42,400 files, 26% more than in 2022; registrations from non-residents rose by over 70% in the same period.
atlas-lu.0090: The 2022 recruitment targets of the Big Four ran from about 500 to 910 each; the sources read give no graduate-only intake figure or conversion rate.
atlas-lu.0091: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens work and study with no permit or labour-market test.
atlas-lu.0092: Declare your arrival at the commune within eight days, then register within three months with your contract, or for students your enrolment, health card and statement of means; both are free, and the registration certificate has no expiry.
atlas-lu.0093: Your employer registers you with social security within eight days, which gives you a 13-digit national number; public transport in second class is free.
atlas-lu.0094: The temporary stay authorisation must be approved before you enter; then the D visa, the arrival declaration at the commune within three working days, a medical check with TB screening, and the biometric permit.
atlas-lu.0095: You may work 15 hours a week on average in term (60 a month) and full time in the holidays.
atlas-lu.0096: A non-EU student with a permit from another EU country can study here up to 360 days without a D visa, after the university notifies the immigration directorate.
atlas-lu.0099: A study internship lasts at most six months; from four weeks on it must pay at least 30% of the minimum wage. A practical internship within two years of graduating pays 40% for weeks 4 to 12 and 75% after.
atlas-lu.0100: Non-EU interns need a trainee authorisation approved before entry, with funds topping the allowance up to the legal minimum.
atlas-lu.0107: Job-search or business permit after a master’s or PhD
atlas-lu.0108: After a master’s or doctorate in Luxembourg, or at the end of a research stay: 12 months, not renewable.
atlas-lu.0109: A job linked to your studies at the qualified minimum wage converts it with no labour-market test.
atlas-lu.0113: Apply at least 30 days before your student permit expires; after it has expired the right is lost.
atlas-lu.0114: A contract of at least six months, a three-year degree or three years of senior experience in the last seven (IT); no labour-market test, a four-year card and immediate family reunion.
atlas-lu.0120: The employer declares the vacancy to the employment agency ADEM: for jobs on the severe-shortage list (IT, engineering, accounting) the certificate comes in five working days with no test; otherwise ADEM checks local job-seekers for seven working days.
atlas-lu.0121: The first permit lasts a year in one sector, then three years in any.
atlas-lu.0124: A hosting agreement with a research body accredited by the ministry, which covers living and return costs up to six months after the project; no labour-market test, and family can join at once.
